content:
Apple has begun beta testing for iOS 27.2, and this update brings a number of important changes and new features. Here's everything you need to know about iOS 27.2, which is expected to roll out to iPhone users as early as next month.

Why iOS 27.2 instead of iOS 27.1?

Apple launched iOS 27 on September 14, bringing a host of new iPhone features including Siri AI. Beta testing for iOS 27.2 began two days later, on September 16.

Why is iOS 27.1 not making a peep?

Apple previously confirmed that the iPhone Duo will come preloaded with iOS 27.1 when it launches on October 23. In other words, iOS 27.1 contains a lot of code relating to the iPhone Duo, and Apple wants to wait until the device officially goes on sale before going public. So iOS 27.1 will be exclusive to the iPhone Duo.

After that, the software roadmaps for the iPhone Duo and other iPhone models will converge, possibly through an iOS 27.2.x update, or possibly iOS 27.3.

So there will be a bit of an awkward period, but ultimately everything will return to normal.

iOS 27.2 new features

Redesigned Health App

At the iPhone 18 Pro launch event, Apple showcased a completely revamped Health App, saying it would launch later this year. This new App has now entered beta testing with iOS 27.2.

The redesigned Health App is divided into three tabs: Insights, Longevity, and Browse. The new App features a brand-new design that dynamically adjusts based on your data, including applications of Apple Intelligence. The Longevity tab adds a "Health age" feature, which uses Apple Watch data to show how your body's metrics compare to your actual age.

The new Health App will most likely not launch alongside iOS 27.2 next month. Apple is starting beta testing of the new App first, before officially opening it up to all users later this year.

Further reading: iOS 27.2 brings major overhaul to Apple Health App, here's a look at every new feature

TV App gains profile functionality

The Apple TV App in iOS 27.2 gains profile support for the first time. This feature has existed on tvOS for years, but is now making its debut on iPhone.

Further reading: iOS 27.2 brings brand-new profile features to Apple TV on iPhone

More Siri AI languages

Siri AI is a marquee new feature of iOS 27, and iOS 27.2 further expands this feature to more users. New language support includes:

  • French
  • Japanese
  • Korean
  • Portuguese
  • Spanish

Group FaceTime gains Dual Capture mode

In iOS 27, Apple added Dual Capture to FaceTime, letting you turn on both the front and rear cameras at the same time. The other party can see not only you, but also what's in front of your camera. iOS 27.2 extends this feature to Group FaceTime calls for the first time.

Dual Capture requires an iPhone 17 or later, and all participants in the call must be running iOS 27.

Further reading: iOS 27.2 makes FaceTime's best new feature even better

Other minor tweaks

  • In Apple Podcasts, the "Up Next" playlist has been renamed "New Episodes." The "Continue Playing" section is now placed right below New Episodes. Episode lists will also adopt matching background colors based on the podcast cover art.
  • In the Music App, some red icons and accent elements have been changed to black.
  • The Call Context feature in iOS 27 displays relevant information directly on the screen when calling a merchant, and it has now been expanded to include anniversary information.
  • The Clock App's alarm interface has minor changes, such as the AM and PM labels being in a smaller font.

Hints at more features coming soon

Finally, the code in iOS 27.2 also hints at several new features that may be coming to iPhone soon, including a new album release countdown feature for Apple Music, third-party app support for Describe a Shortcut, and new themes for CarPlay Ultra. iOS 27.2 also shows that Apple continues to develop iPhone anti-robbery features.

These features are not currently enabled in iOS 27.2, but the code shows that Apple is actively developing them internally.

iOS 27.2 release date

iOS 27.2 is expected to officially launch for iPhone users sometime in October. Apple has promised that Siri AI will support new languages in October, and iOS 27.2 adds exactly these new languages, so the update must roll out before November for Apple to deliver on its promise.

Summary

Are you using iOS 27.2 beta? Have you found any useful new features? What are your thoughts on the new Health App? Feel free to share with us in the comments.
